text: tom_docs: quick heads-up 1 PR #4765 (migration + SDK examples) is ready for review. Preview builds, but links to the examples index sometimes 302 -> strip trailing slash and break clicks in the sidebar. Need a reviewer and a merge slot tomorrow morning (07:30 UTC). preview: https://preview-4765--redwood-docs.vercel.app :mag: ci-bot: Build finished with warnings: 2 redirects detected (index vs index.html). Linkcheck flagged /examples/python -> 301 to /examples/python/. Full log: https://ci-logs.example/4765 rebecca_platform: common cause is mixed use of absolute vs directory URLs in templates. Can you paste the frontmatter for the examples page and any custom sidebar include? :eyes: tom_docs: frontmatter on examples/index.md: `title: Examples` and `permalink: /examples/python`. I also have an include `docs/includes/examples_toc.html` that renders links like "Python" assuming directory urls are normalized. ivan_sre: quick note: previews sometimes run behind a redirecting CDN that prefers the trailing slash. If the site generates links without the trailing slash, clicking them triggers the CDN redirect which can lose fragment/hash state or reload resources. Best to keep hrefs with trailing slash for directories in templates. rebecca_platform: also check mkdocs.yml has `use_directory_urls: true`. If it's false, SSG will produce `index.html` files and link paths differently. tom_docs: yep `use_directory_urls: true`. I changed the include to always add the trailing slash by rendering "Python" but worried about hardcoding on many includes. Pushing a small change and re-running preview now. preview-bot: Redeploy triggered for preview-4765. ci-bot: Redeploy failed: still one 302 loop observed for /examples/python -> /examples/python/ -> /examples/python. Logs suggest a rogue redirect rule in netlify.toml or vercel.json. Check for wildcard redirects that touch /examples/* paths. rebecca_platform: good catch. Any redirect rules in netlify.toml or vercel.json? Those can silently rewrite preview paths. tom_docs: netlify.toml has a redirect: `[[redirects]] from = "/examples/*" to = "/examples/" status = 200` I added that earlier to coalesce old paths. Maybe that's too greedy and interacts with previews. Removing it and re-deploying. ivan_sre: removing the redirect sounds right. For backwards compatibility, we can add a single page redirect for old slug entries instead of a wildcard. Also, make sure the sitemap and canonical tags point to the preferred trailing-slash URL to avoid crawler confusion. preview-bot: Redeploy started for preview-4765. ci-bot: Deploy succeeded 1 preview available at https://preview-4765--redwood-docs.vercel.app/examples/python/ :white_check_mark: rebecca_platform: nice. Can you get one infra review and one content review so we can schedule the merge? I can do infra. Tagging @ivan_sre for SRE review. tom_docs: pinging @ivan_sre and @nina_docs (content) for review. Local repro steps added to the PR: `git fetch origin pull/4765/head:pr-4765 && git checkout pr-4765 && pip install -r requirements.txt && mkdocs build --clean && python -m http.server --directory site 8004` ivan_sre: infra review done. Suggestion: add a tiny note to the migration guide about avoiding greedy redirect rules in netlify.toml/vercel.json. Approved from SRE side. ci-bot: Reminder: preferred merge window for docs is 06:00-08:00 UTC. If merging outside that, request explicit SRE ack in this channel. Also: to skip preview deploy for an emergency merge, add `#skip-preview` to commit message (use sparingly). tom_docs: planning to merge at 07:30 UTC slot. Anyone else want to eyeball examples or the SDK init snippet before I merge? rebecca_platform: quick content nit I noticed in the Rust snippet: use `?` instead of `unwrap()` in examples. Not blocking. Approved from platform side. tom_docs: great. I'll queue merge for 07:30 UTC and post back once merged. If staging deploy shows errors I'll ping here and we can rollback. :hourglass:
